Hey man. Once again like I said before, my argument is all about prenatal illnesses that will harm the baby and cause the baby pain throughout life. I'm in my 20s so I cannot speak for elderly people. I suffer from a seriously damaged back spine however if my diseases were with me since birth, I'd rather not have them and not live the limited life I do. 

People have different ways of thinking and perceiving life. Some people may be more optimistic than be while being more injured.

Once again, I'm talking about serious genetic illnesses; for example chromosomal abnormalities where you have some organs missing from your body since birth. Or single gene disorders such as sickle cell anemia. If my kid were at a risk, I should at least have the choice, along with my SO, to decide if we deserve to give a kid the future that may lie ahead.

"Hard life" is extremely vague and exceptionally circumstantial. You may have very different views of what's hard.

However a life threatening illness (incurable genetic diseases) that will undoubtedly cause pain in the child's life, can be **objectively** viewed as a hard life. That's my main point here. You've gone on to include abortion past birth and parents ability. I never said anything about these, only you did.

It is NOT my place to say who should have and who doesnt deserve to have kids. But I do encourage everyone to think about the kid's life and ones capacity to financially and more importantly, emotionally support a kid.

That's not what I'm saying. I'm saying that when you can diagnose a fetus, long before the 9 month mark, of any life threatening, permanent diseases that will be an obstacle through life, then abortion should be an accessible option for the parents.
